hero.title: Assessment your people can trust
hero.lead: Run established tests and questionnaires as rounds, get scored reports the moment people finish, and see how teams compare. Consent, privacy and a psychologist's judgement are built in, not bolted on.
hero.note: No card needed. You move to the Free plan when the trial ends, and keep your data.

features.title: What Calibre does
features.lead: Everything between choosing an instrument and reading the result, without paper forms or spreadsheets.

library.title: A validated library
library.text: Ability tests, personality questionnaires and clinical screens in English and Russian, ready to send. Build your own in the studio.

rounds.title: Rounds, not links
rounds.text: Send a set of instruments to a team with a due date. Calibre sends the invitations and reminders, and people sign in with a one-time link.

reports.title: Reports that read like documents
reports.text: Raw scores, T-scores and stens with an interpretation for every scale. Add background and a conclusion, then print or export.

analytics.title: Team analytics
analytics.text: Compare a person with their team and the organization, follow change between rounds, and save the views you use.

trust.title: Built for sensitive data
trust.lead: Psychological results deserve more care than an ordinary HR form.

consent.title: Consent first
consent.text: People read a plain-language privacy notice and agree to it before their first assessment.

access.title: Private by default
access.text: Only the staff you choose see answers and scores. Colleagues never do.

judgement.title: Support, not diagnosis
judgement.text: Results inform a qualified specialist's judgement and never replace it.

clinical.title: Clinical screens stay clinical
clinical.text: Depression, anxiety and similar screens, and their results, are visible only to psychologists and the workspace owner.

retention.title: Kept only as long as needed
retention.text: Set how long results are kept. Every view and change is written to an audit log.

pick.title: Choose instruments
pick.text: Pick from the library or build your own, and choose the people or teams to assess.

send.title: People take them online
send.text: Invitations and reminders go out by email. Answers save as people go, on any phone or computer.

read.title: Read the results
read.text: Reports are ready the moment someone finishes, and the round shows who is still to go.

library.title: From the library
library.lead: A few of the instruments you can send on day one. Each page explains what it measures and when to use it.

plans.title: Priced by the people you assess
plans.lead: Every plan includes staff seats. You pay for the number of people who take an assessment in a year.

cta.title: Run your first round this week

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lead: Calibre is used by your organization to run psychological questionnaires and tests. This notice explains what is collected, who can see it and what you can do about it.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.text: Your profile (name, email, date of birth, team, position and, if an administrator adds one, a photo), the answers you give, and the scores and interpretations calculated from them.

purpose.title: Why
purpose.text: To support hiring, development and well-being decisions in your organization. Results are one input for a qualified specialist and are never a medical diagnosis on their own.

access.title: Who can see it
access.text: Only people your organization authorises, such as HR specialists and psychologists. Results of clinical and wellbeing screens are visible only to psychologists and the organization’s owner. Other employees cannot see your answers or results.

storage.title: How long it is kept
storage.text: Until your organization's retention period ends, you leave the organization or an administrator removes you; then your answers, results and reports there are deleted. Who opened your results is recorded and kept for two years.

rights.title: Your choices
rights.text: Taking part is voluntary. You can stop any questionnaire or test before finishing it, download a copy of your data or withdraw your consent from your account page, and ask your HR team to correct or delete your data.

privacy.controller: Your organization is responsible for how this data is used. Contact your HR team with any questions.

pricing.metaDescription: Calibre plans for HR teams: Free, Team, Business and Enterprise, priced by the number of people you assess each year. 14-day free trial, no card needed.
pricing.title: Pay for the people you assess, not for seats
pricing.lead: Start with a 14-day trial of Business. When it ends you move to Free and keep everything, unless you choose a plan.
pricing.seats: {count, plural, one {# staff seat} other {# staff seats}}

free.name: Free
free.tagline: Try it with a small team

pricing.note: Prices are in euros and exclude VAT. Our reseller Paddle handles payment, tax and invoices.

respondent.a: Anyone who submits at least one test or questionnaire in your billing year, counted once however many assessments they take. Staff who only review results don't count.

limit.q: What happens if we go over our limit?
limit.a: A round that is already running is never cut off. When you reach your limit we let you know, and you can upgrade or wait for the next billing year.

trial.a: Every new workspace gets 14 days of Business without a card. When it ends you move to Free unless you choose a plan, and nothing is deleted.

billing.a: Our orders are processed by Paddle, who act as the reseller and merchant of record. Paddle handles payment, VAT and sales tax, and sends the invoices.

cancel.q: Can we cancel or get a refund?
cancel.a: You can cancel at any time and keep your plan to the end of the period you paid for. Our refund policy explains when you can get your money back.

privacy.q: Are privacy features behind a paywall?
privacy.a: No. Consent, data export, erasure and withdrawal of consent work on every plan, including Free.

product.metaDescription: How Calibre runs psychological assessment for HR teams: rounds, a calm respondent experience, scored reports, team analytics, a studio for your own instruments and privacy controls.
product.title: From the first invitation to the final report
product.lead: A tour of Calibre, in the order you'll use it.

rounds.title: Rounds
rounds.lead: An assessment is a round: a set of instruments, the people who take them and a due date.
points: Send to people or whole teams, and add candidates by email.
Invitations and reminders go out on their own. Nobody needs a password.
The round shows who has finished, who is late and what needs checking.

respondents.title: For the person taking it
respondents.lead: Answering should feel calm, private and quick, on any device.
points: One question at a time, in large type, with keyboard shortcuts.
Answers save as people go, so they can stop and come back.
They see your organization's name, not ours, and a clear privacy notice before they start.

reports.title: Reports
reports.lead: Scores arrive the moment someone finishes, laid out like a document you can hand to a manager.
points: Raw scores, T-scores and stens with an interpretation for every scale.
Background, conclusion and recommendations written by your psychologist.
Prints cleanly on A4 or Letter, and exports to CSV.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.lead: See patterns across people without losing sight of the person.
points: Compare a person with their team and the whole organization on the same scale.
Follow change between rounds and spot large shifts.
Save the filters you use, and hide groups too small to stay anonymous.

studio.title: Studio
studio.lead: Build your own tests and questionnaires, or adapt a copy of one from the library.
points: Write questions, choices and scoring keys, and preview them as respondents will see them.
Publish versions, so results always match the questions that were asked.

privacy.title: Privacy and control
privacy.lead: Psychological data is sensitive, so the controls are part of the product, not an add-on.
points: Roles decide who sees what. Clinical screens are for psychologists and the owner only.
Consent before the first assessment, and export or erasure on request.
Retention periods and an audit log of every view and change.

instruments.metaDescription: The psychological tests and questionnaires in the Calibre library: what each one measures, how long it takes and when HR teams use it.
instruments.title: Instruments
instruments.lead: Established tests and questionnaires you can send from Calibre, scored automatically and interpreted scale by scale.
instruments.scoringValue: Automatic, with stens and an interpretation
instruments.itemsNote: We don't publish the questions, so the instrument stays valid for the people who take it.
instruments.clinicalNote: The library also includes clinical screens, such as anxiety and depression scales. They are available to psychologists on the Business plan and are not listed publicly.

cta.title: Send it to your team
cta.text: Start a free trial and send this instrument in a round today.

analogies.name: Analogies
analogies.summary: A verbal reasoning test: find the pair of words linked in the same way as an example pair.
analogies.measures: Logical thinking with words: seeing how concepts relate, and applying the same relation to new ones. It is a quick measure of general reasoning ability.
analogies.use: Selection and development for roles where people reason with information, such as analysts, specialists and managers. Use it alongside other evidence, never on its own.

arithmetic.name: Arithmetic
arithmetic.summary: A timed test of mental arithmetic: adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing without a calculator.
arithmetic.measures: Speed and accuracy with numbers, and the ability to stay focused under time pressure.
arithmetic.use: Roles that work with figures every day, such as finance, operations, sales and customer service. Retesting is limited so repeated attempts don't inflate the score.

patterns.name: Patterns
patterns.summary: Find the words that follow a given rule about their order and number of letters.
patterns.measures: Attention, concentration and the ability to spot rules and regularities quickly.
patterns.use: Roles that need careful, accurate work with detail, such as administration, quality control and data entry.

communication-and-organisation.name: Communication and organisation
communication-and-organisation.summary: A questionnaire on how readily someone makes contact with people and takes charge of organizing them.
communication-and-organisation.measures: Two scales: communicative tendencies (making and keeping contact, ease in groups) and organizational tendencies (taking initiative, organizing others, making decisions).
communication-and-organisation.use: Teams, roles with a lot of contact with people, and early spotting of future team leads.

leadership.name: Leadership
leadership.summary: A short questionnaire on the personal qualities that make leading others come naturally.
leadership.measures: The tendency to take the lead: confidence, initiative, the wish to influence others and to take responsibility for a group.
leadership.use: Leadership programs, succession planning and conversations about career direction.

risk-readiness.name: Readiness to take risks
risk-readiness.summary: Schubert's questionnaire on how willing someone is to take risks in everyday and work situations.
risk-readiness.measures: Where someone sits between caution and boldness when a situation is uncertain.
risk-readiness.use: Roles where the balance between caution and initiative matters, such as sales, safety and leadership, and team conversations about decision styles.
